text: Bangladesh Unrest: Dhaka on Edge as Yunus’ Special Assistant Quits | Live-N18LBangladesh’s capital Dhaka is on high alert as political tensions escalate amid growing street unrest and allegations of radical pressure on the interim administration led by Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus. The situation intensified after Khoda Baksh Chowdhury, Special Assistant to the Chief Adviser, resigned, triggering fresh questions over governance and control ahead of the crucial February 12 polls. Large-scale demonstrations and calls by Islamist groups have raised concerns about law and order, political stability, and the government’s ability to rein in radical elements. Critics allege that the Yunus administration is under pressure from hardline groups, while supporters argue the government is navigating an extremely volatile transition period. The resignation of a senior aide has added to the uncertainty, with opposition voices claiming it reflects deeper cracks within the interim setup. As unrest simmers on the streets of Dhaka, authorities insist security forces are monitoring the situation closely. #BreakingNews #Bangladesh #dhaka n18oc_live n18oc_world News18 Mobile App - https://onelink.to/desc-youtube
